messages:
alex: noticed a spike of 502+ and LB healthcheck failures for eu-west gpu-pool around 10:34 UTC. pods still Ready but hitting conn resets :eyes:

infra-bot: Deploy v3.2.1 started by @ci (build-3344) — 10:28 UTC

sam: any changes to ingress or lb config? 

alex: I rolled a small ingress rule PR 30m ago to tighten allowed source cidrs for the internal proxy. NACLs unchanged. 

maria: Can you paste the security group rules and the ELB target group healthcheck config? suspecting ephemeral port / SNAT mapping issues.

alex:
```
# sg-internal-proxy
ingress:
  - proto: tcp
    ports: 50000-50010
    src: 10.0.0.0/16
    desc: proxy health
```
ELB TG health: port 50001, path /_hc, interval 10s, healthy threshold 3

gwen: Wait, SG only allows a tiny ephemeral range (50000-50010) — LB and kube-proxy SNAT will use ports > 32768 typically. That range looks wrong. :thinking_face:

sam: Also check node NAT and AWS NAT gateway source port translation. If we have connection churn from model downloads and bursts, NAT port exhaustion can cause source ports to be reused/mapped outside that SG range.

alex: running tcpdump on node-03 now; if healthchecks from ELB appear from source ports outside 50000-50010, SG will drop them. 

infra-bot: tcpdump saved to s3://redwood-debug/tcpdump/node-03-2045678901.pcap

alex: tcpdump shows incoming probes from 34.198.12.7:56321 -> 10.8.4.12:50001 (reset). So source port 56321.

maria: That's the problem — SG allowed only 50000-50010. How did that range get introduced? I think previous infra hardening PR intended to lock down ephemeral ports for a different ALB. 

gwen: Quick mitigation: expand SG to allow ephemeral range 32768-61000 for the internal proxy, or set ELB to use proxy protocol / preserve client IP so healthchecks originate differently.

sam: Also consider setting service.spec.externalTrafficPolicy=Local on k8s svc so LB health checks target node local pods instead of being SNATed through kube-proxy.

alex: temporary sg change applied (allowed 32768-61000) — applying and monitoring. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: SG updated sg-0a1b2c3d — rule added 32768-61000 tcp

gwen: Can we add a regression alert that flags SG rules with tiny ephemeral ranges for any proxy/health ports? This will bite us again.

maria: opened ticket INFRA-823 to audit SGs and NACLs across regions and to enforce policy. tagging @security @platform. link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-823

alex: healthchecks back to healthy 2/3 after SG change. will follow up with PR to revert to correct rules and document required ranges. Thanks all :fire:

sam: nice catch. we should also add a test in the deploy pipeline that simulates LB health probes and verifies SG/NACL allow them.

gwen: agreed. also check nat-gateway metrics for port exhaustion spikes around the incident window.

alex: notes: root cause = overly restrictive SG ephemeral port range introduced by previous harden PR; compounded by SNAT mapping. Action items in INFRA-823.
